reviews.title: AVOID IF YOU ACTUALLY WANT TO KEEP YOUR MONEY – Hidden fees will destroy your margins
reviews.text:
I’ve used Invoice Simple for years with no issues when I was only creating invoices and getting paid by cash, check, or direct bank transfer. The app itself is fine for basic invoicing.
The moment I accepted my first payment through their built-in payment processing, everything went wrong.
A single $1,500 invoice ended up costing me almost $150 in fees — and my customer was double-charged on their card too. I was hit with four separate charges on the same transaction (processing fee, service fee, “platform” fee, and some other mystery charge). That’s a 10% bite out of one job.
They advertise this as “small-business friendly” and “simple, low-cost payments,” but 10% on every transaction is absolutely predatory for freelancers, contractors, and small businesses who already run on thin margins. Stripe, Square, PayPal — literally every other processor — charges 2.9% + $0.30 or less. Invoice Simple is ripping people off and hiding it behind multiple stacked fees.
If you only need to create and email/pdf invoices that get paid outside the app, it’s okay. The second you turn on their payment processing, run away. There are dozens of better, truly affordable options that won’t punish you for getting paid.
Small business owners: do not make the same mistake I did. Look elsewhere for payment processing.
1 star only because zero isn’t an option.
Feel free to tweak any part of it (add your business type or exact fee breakdown if you have screenshots), but this version is emotional, factual, and written to rank high and warn others effectively. Post it on both the App Store and Google Play if you can — the more visible, the better.

reviews.title: Misleading support, no Stripe access, poor experience for real businesses
reviews.text:
I upgraded to Premium based on Invoice Simple’s claim that Stripe would be available — which was completely fine at the time, since I was actively testing invoicing apps and CRMs for my company. Stripe is an essential platform for us, so I was optimistic when I saw it listed.

Three weeks later, it’s still not available. I’ve reached out to support multiple times and still haven’t received a clear answer. One rep told me, “Don’t worry, it will be available after you upgrade.” Another said, “Hang tight, I’ll look into this,” then closed the chat after 30 minutes with no resolution.

I submitted screenshots, asked direct questions, and gave the team every chance to resolve it — but nothing changed. If this had happened once or twice, I’d understand. But nearly a dozen support attempts, weeks of waiting, and zero access to Stripe — all while paying for premium — is unacceptable.

Bottom line: if you’re a business that relies on Stripe or expects reliable support, look elsewhere. This platform failed on both fronts.

reviews.title: App started off great until recently. Will cost you money.
reviews.text: We’ve had this app for almost 5 years. They were great until this past year. They’ve been starting to make updates that are causing bugs and glitches that can cost a business a lot of money. They recently integrated Stripe into their payment system and they have a feature that lets you pass the processing fees on to the customer. The settings are straightforward and you can switch that feature on or off. We always keep it on because we generally push customers to use other forms of payment that don’t includes fees, but if there’s no other way, they can pay through this app. Recently we had a customer make a payment over $1,000 and there was a hiccup between Invoice and Stripe. They deducted the percentage from our earnings after the customer had already taken his vehicle and left. So we message their support teams and they quickly jump to find a way to pin this on us. Saying we switched the setting off (which you’d have to go out of your way to do) and then saying we don’t know what invoice we’re even talking about. Eventually the agent by the name of Nigel ghosted me for several days and even after I followed up for an update, he left my messages on seen back to back. These guys would rather lose a loyal customer that has never batted an eye when they do their yearly price increases, than reimburse a $40 fee they never should’ve taken in the first place. Now if that’s what they do with a $1,000 transaction… we have transactions of up to $20,000 and sometimes it’s not even profit, but just a customer sending us money for us to place a parts order for them. Imagine being forced to pay $800 out of your pocket for a customer’s parts because your own payment processor screwed you. We will be switching over to Square and leaving this review up if they don’t correct their mistake.
